metric.name: frame_ui_time_p95_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur, a.jank_type
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  frames AS (
    SELECT * FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT s.dur AS ns, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY s.dur) AS rank,
      count(*) OVER () AS n
    FROM android_frames_choreographer_do_frame AS d
    JOIN slice AS s USING (id)
    WHERE d.ui_thread_utid IN (SELECT ui_thread_utid FROM frames)
  )
SELECT (SELECT ns / 1e6 FROM ranked WHERE rank = (n * 95 + 99) / 100) AS value

claims.text: The app UI-thread 95th-percentile frame time increased from 8.3585 ms in baseline to 13.957625 ms in current, a 5.599125 ms increase.

claims.text: The localized change is on the app's UI thread: its maximum top-level traversal slice increased from 9.115416 ms in baseline to 18.846833 ms in current.

citations.sql:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
SELECT s.name, s.ts, s.dur / 1e6 AS dur_ms
FROM slice AS s
JOIN thread_track AS tt ON tt.id = s.track_id
JOIN thread AS t ON t.utid = tt.utid
WHERE t.name = 'example.jetnews' AND s.name = 'traversal'
ORDER BY s.dur DESC
LIMIT 10;

INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;

WHERE t.name = 'example.jetnews' AND s.name = 'traversal'
ORDER BY s.dur DESC
LIMIT 10;

claims.text: Commit 9d695fef3c759e53d1bb01327b328a5d5e30bb87 changed PostCards.kt's bookmark click handler to call Thread.sleep after toggling a favorite, matching the added UI-thread traversal cost and making it the likely cause within the supplied range.
The blocking bookmark-handler lines were introduced by commit 9d695fef3c759e53d1bb01327b328a5d5e30bb87, rather than by the surrounding commits.

caveats: the current trace's build was debuggable (run metadata: debuggable), so ART ran it with fewer optimisations and its timings overstate a release build's
This conclusion compares one capture per side, so some of the delta may be run-to-run noise.
The traces were captured on an emulator and the current build was debuggable, which can affect absolute performance.
